pipelines.name: build-kb
pipelines.description: Build ONLY the knowledge base from a client's raw reference files, then STOP — this pipeline generates no document, no config, no other deliverable. It runs kb-builder alone to extract the delivery team's format, boilerplate, and product knowledge into a reusable KB, and returns that KB. Use it whenever the user wants JUST the KB and has NOT asked for a specific deliverable in the same request — e.g. 'build the KB for this client', 'onboard this client', 'set up the generator'. The KB it produces is the seed for every generation pipeline, so keep the session id it reports: later, pass that id as `seed_session_id` to document-from-kb or config-from-kb to generate a deliverable, or to output-feedback to refine the KB. Do NOT reach for document-agent or config-generator when the user only wants a KB — those append a generator step the user did not ask for.

pipelines.name: document-agent
pipelines.description: Produce a finished business document from raw reference files end to end. Runs kb-builder to extract the team's format and product knowledge into a KB, then document-generator to write and render the final document (PDF or DOCX) directly from that KB. This builds the KB AND produces a document in one run — so use it only when the user wants the finished document now. If the user wants ONLY the KB and no document yet, use build-kb instead; if the KB was already built by an earlier run, use document-from-kb to skip rebuilding it.
triggers: generate a document from reference files
build a document from samples
create SOW from reference documents
create BRD from sample documents
generate HLD from references
generate a document end to end
build KB and generate the document
produce a document from these references

pipelines.name: document-from-kb
pipelines.description: Generate a finished business document (SOW, BRD, HLD, proposal, etc.) from an EXISTING knowledge base, WITHOUT rebuilding it. Use when the KB was already built by an earlier run and you just want another document from it for a new deal. This is the 'straight to generation' path that skips the kb-builder phase of document-agent. Point at the KB via `seed_session_id` — pass the pipeline session id of the earlier run that built the KB (the one it reported on completion); the server recovers that run's KB bucket from it automatically, so it is the only id you need. Upload the per-deal MOM/brief via `r2_keys`/`urls` and describe the deal in `context`. The KB is staged in as read-only reference and the finished document is written to its own fresh output bucket — the KB is never modified.

pipelines.name: config-generator
pipelines.description: Generate a final configuration file (JSON, XML, YAML, NodeFlow, etc.) from raw reference documents end to end. Runs kb-builder to extract the platform's grammar and rules into a KB, then config-agent to produce and validate the config against that KB. This builds the KB AND produces a config in one run — so use it only when the user wants the finished config now. If the user wants ONLY the KB and no config yet, use build-kb instead; if the KB was already built by an earlier run, use config-from-kb to skip rebuilding it.

generate config
build config

generate YAML config
create configuration

pipelines.name: config-from-kb
pipelines.description: Generate a structured config (JSON, XML, YAML, NodeFlow, etc.) from an EXISTING knowledge base, WITHOUT rebuilding it. Use when the KB was already built by an earlier run and you just want another config from it for a new deal or scenario. This is the 'straight to generation' path that skips the kb-builder phase of config-generator. Point at the KB via `seed_session_id` — pass the pipeline session id of the earlier run that built the KB (the one it reported on completion); the server recovers that run's KB bucket from it automatically, so it is the only id you need. Upload the per-deal SOW/brief via `r2_keys`/`urls` and describe what to build in `context`. The KB is staged in as read-only reference and the generated config is written to its own fresh output bucket — the KB is never modified.

pipelines.name: output-feedback
pipelines.description: Turn a user's complaint about a generated OUTPUT into approved amendments to the knowledge base behind it, so the next generation is better. The user talks about the OUTPUT — 'the SOW is off-brand', 'the document missed a section', 'the config has the wrong value' — and need NOT mention the KB at all; this flow deliberately routes the fix to the KB, because every generator skill reads the KB at runtime, so correcting the KB is what actually fixes future outputs. Point it at the run whose output is at fault via `seed_session_id` — the pipeline session id that run reported on completion; the server resolves that run's KB bucket from it and refines it in place — and pass the flagged issues as `context`; optionally attach the defective output and/or a corrected version as uploads (r2_keys/urls). Runs diagnose-bug in KB mode to analyse the KB against the feedback and propose amendments for review (adding a fact the KB never recorded, correcting one it recorded wrongly, or flagging a rule the KB already states correctly as a generator defect rather than restating it), then apply-fixes in KB mode to write the approved amendments back into that same KB in place. The KB is edited on disk with no git commit; the amended KB is written back into its own outputs/mcp bucket in place so every skill that reads it at runtime picks up the improvement.
triggers: the SOW you generated was wrong
the document you produced is off-brand or incomplete
the generated output missed something

the config came out wrong
